content.text: {"headline":"Approve P0: no action needed. Service is predicted at 90.7% for 11:45-19:45, above the 80% target.","why":"General-queue calls are running 27–47% above forecast since 09:45 (1,106 vs 864 so far, +28%). The rise is spread across all call reasons, and nothing in the feeds explains it: no incidents, no marketing sends, normal absence. Even so, current staffing is predicted to hold 90.7% over the window (general 89.5%, payments 91.9%) with 2.1% abandons. Rest of day is 90.3%. At zero cost with no policy issues, no action is the cheapest plan that meets target.","trade_offs":["P1 (break shifts and evening callback, ₹0) is no better: 90.3% overall. It lowers general to 87.4% while lifting payments to 93.2%, so it moves pressure onto the surging queue.","P2 (chat deflection, break delay, callback, overtime, ₹864) gives a small gain to 91.5% (general 90.7%) and 1.9% abandons.","P3 (break shifts plus 20 overtime offers, ₹2,160) is strongest at 92.5% and 1.7% abandons. That is about 2 points over doing nothing at the highest cost and with the most disruption to agents."],"watch":"The cause of the surge is unknown, so keep an eye on general-queue volume against forecast. If it keeps climbing, general (89.5%) is the queue closest to slipping, and P2 is the cheapest ready fallback. Ask marketing about a possible unlisted offer: new_offer_enquiry is at 36 vs 19 expected."}
